deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's account of eigenvalue–singular-value inequalities for operators on Hilbert space. It sits inside his 1953 work on Fredholm theory and tensor products. Notation: λ_i are the eigenvalues of u, with |λ_1| ≥ |λ_2| ≥ ..., counted with multiplicity. ρ_i are the singular values of u, that is, the eigenvalues of (u*u)^{1/2}, in decreasing order.

The page builds on two facts.
- **Weyl's multiplicative inequalities:** |λ_1⋯λ_k| ≤ ρ_1⋯ρ_k for every k.
- **Previous page:** Grothendieck had shown that for f defined on ρ>0 with f(e^t) convex, F(ρ_1,…,ρ_n) = Σ f(ρ_i) is symmetric and convex in the logarithms of its arguments. Hence F satisfies the hypotheses of his abstract 'Theorem 1 / Corollary 1'.

**(18)–(19).** If f is in addition increasing and continuous at 0, then Σ_{i≤n} f(|λ_i|) ≤ Σ_{i≤n} f(ρ_i) for every n. In infinite dimension, letting n→∞ gives: convergence of Σ f(ρ_i) implies convergence of Σ f(|λ_i|), with Σ f(|λ_i|) ≤ Σ f(ρ_i). This is Weyl's majorant theorem (1949).

**Corollary 2.** Take f(x) = x^p with p>0. For a compact u, Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ ρ_i^p, both for partial sums and for the full series, where the right side may be infinite.

**Corollary 3.** Take p=1 and p=2.
- If u is a 'Fredholm' operator (trace class/nuclear), its eigenvalues are summable and Σ|λ_i| ≤ ‖u‖_1.
- If u is Hilbert–Schmidt, its eigenvalues are square-summable and (Σ|λ_i|²)^{1/2} ≤ ‖u‖_2.

**Corollary 4 (finite dimension n, set in smaller type).** Let F be a function of n positive arguments with F(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) convex, not necessarily increasing. If F is symmetric and increasing, then F(|λ_1|,…,|λ_n|) ≤ F(ρ_1,…,ρ_n). The proof starts from Weyl's inequalities |λ_1⋯λ_k| ≤ ρ_1⋯ρ_k for k ≤ n.

The next page adds the equality |λ_1⋯λ_n| = |det u| = ρ_1⋯ρ_n. This turns weak log-majorization into log-majorization, so for invertible u the monotonicity hypothesis can be dropped. A limiting argument then handles the general case under continuity. From this he passes to symmetric gauge functions ('normes de Schatten') N(|λ|) ≤ N(ρ).

What this serves: controlling the eigenvalues of nuclear and Hilbert–Schmidt operators, as needed for his Fredholm theory and the trace/determinant work in Produits tensoriels topologiques and La théorie de Fredholm.
errors: (20)/(21) write Σρ_i^p = ‖u‖_p. But (22) uses (Σ|λ_i|²)^{1/2} ≤ ‖u‖_2, i.e. ‖u‖_p = (Σρ_i^p)^{1/p}. The consistent statement is Σρ_i^p = ‖u‖_p^p. Harmless for p=1, a slip otherwise.
In (19) the summation indices are inconsistent: i=1 on the left, i=0 on the right.

Corollary 4 is stated loosely: it says 'pas forcément croissante' and then also assumes 'croissante'. The intended dichotomy appears on the next page. Without monotonicity the inequality holds for invertible u, via det equality and majorization. With monotonicity and continuity it holds for all u.

ideas.what: Σ f(|λ_i|) ≤ Σ f(ρ_i) for f(e^t) convex and increasing, partial sums and infinite series, for compact operators
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's majorant theorem (weak log-majorization of eigenvalues by singular values)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck uses such eigenvalue estimates in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955) and La théorie de Fredholm (1956); exact statement there unsure

ideas.what: Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ s_i^p; trace class implies summable eigenvalues, Hilbert–Schmidt implies square-summable eigenvalues
For symmetric F convex in the logarithms of its arguments, F(|λ|) ≤ F(ρ); for invertible u the monotonicity can be dropped using |det u| = Πρ_i; extension to symmetric gauge functions
ideas.modern_name: Log-majorization / Schur-convexity results; Ky Fan and Horn for symmetric gauge functions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful re-derivation of Weyl's 1949 eigenvalue/singular-value inequalities and their standard corollaries, in Grothendieck's own convexity framework. It is all classical and in the literature; it is of interest only as documentation of his 1953 preparation for the Fredholm/nuclear operator work.
transcription_corrections: Corollary 3: 'op. de Fredholm' here means trace class/nuclear; 'H.-S.' means Hilbert–Schmidt.
The second formula labelled (21) under Corollary 3 should be read as a separate numbering, (21)/(22) in the image, not a duplicate of the earlier (21).
Left margin near Corollary 4 reads 'petit caractère' (typesetting instruction: print in small type).
